clue.text: Humanitarian crisis caused by a 25 in unoccupied France

indicators.note: a word left unoccupied has its interior emptied, keeping only the two letters at its ends
one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of France
25 across is DESPOT, and Idi Amin of Uganda was a notorious one

explanation.surface: A disaster caused by a tyrant in a France emptied of its people.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 25 across, DESPOT; 'a 25' asks for an example of one, Idi Amin. He sits inside F_E to give FAMINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A famine is a severe food shortage, a classic example of a humanitarian emergency affecting whole populations.

clue.text: Team getting victory launched revolutionary air-to-air missile

indicators.note: something launched goes upwards, and in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a side is a sports team
a win is a victory
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A team celebrating a win fires off a revolutionary new missile.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sidewinder is a well-known heat-seeking missile fired by one aircraft at another.

clue.text: English king upset large part of church before start of divorce is declined

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset suggests turning something upside down, so the letters read upwards
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
before tells you the pieces are placed one after another in this order

blocks.note: E for English and R for rex, king
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the apse is the rounded end of a church
the opening letter of divorce

explanation.surface: An English king overturns the church's authority before a divorce, as Henry VIII famously did.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Henry VIII breaking with Rome to divorce; 'upset' really just flips the royal cipher, and 'large part of church' is two pieces, L plus the curved end.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into a worse condition, so relapsed means having worsened or deteriorated.

clue.text: Cop guarding god leaving hospital in Texas city

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so one piece goes around the other
when something is leaving, it is taken away from the word

blocks.note: DS is a Detective Sergeant
Allah is God in Islam
H is the map symbol for hospital

explanation.surface: A police officer protects a deity who has just walked out of a Texan hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed H is the map symbol for a hospital, a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a large city in the US state of Texas, famous for its oil and its television soap.

clue.text: Menial worker follows lad smuggling diamonds

indicators.note: a smuggler hides goods inside something, so one piece is concealed within another

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them
a lad is a boy
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A lowly worker tails a youth who is smuggling diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody is British slang for someone given all the boring, menial jobs, a drudge or general skivvy.

clue.text: Drug used in game turned up in sweet

indicators.note: something used in another thing is put inside it
in a down clue, turned up means flipped to read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: pool is a cue game played on a table
a pill is a dose of a drug

explanation.surface: Drugs smuggled into a game end up hidden in a piece of confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first and the whole result is then read upwards, as 'turned up' in a down clue means flipping the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard candy on a stick, a type of confectionery.

clue.text: Beautiful lass taking drug to party

indicators.note: a word taking something in holds it within its letters

blocks.note: fine can mean beautiful or handsome
gal is a colloquial word for a girl
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A pretty young woman takes drugs before heading to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'party' a celebration; it is an Irish political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine Gael is one of the main political parties in the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Creatures eaten by giant spiders

indicators.note: something eaten by other words is swallowed inside them, concealed in the run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of giant and the start of spiders

explanation.surface: Small creatures being devoured by huge spiders.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants are insects, and insects are living creatures, so a general word stands for the specific one.

clue.text: Lecturer joining end of impromptu party game

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is kept
joining means the pieces link together one after another

blocks.note: L is a standard abbreviation for lecturer
the final letter of impromptu
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: A lecturer turns up at a spontaneous party and joins in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple board game where players race counters around the board by throwing dice.

clue.text: Small drink that's for shooting party's guide in Scotland

blocks.note: a gill is a small measure of liquor, a quarter of a pint
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A little dram handed out to the guide leading a Highland shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gillie is a Scottish attendant who assists people out hunting, stalking deer or fishing.

clue.text: Left share covered by legal agreement

indicators.note: something covered by another thing is wrapped inside it

blocks.note: a deed is a signed legal document
a part is a share or portion

explanation.surface: Someone's portion of an estate laid down in a legal contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like an inheritance in this surface; it is the past tense of leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To have departed is to have gone away, the same meaning as left as the past of leave.

clue.text: Boy cycles to end of platform to help Southern train attendants

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: b is a dictionary abbreviation for boy
to cycle is to ride a bike
the last letter of platform
aid is help
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A boy cycles to the far end of the station platform to help passengers onto a Southern train.
explanation.walkthrough: Southern is also the name of a British rail operator, which strengthens the railway picture. The train here is the long tail of a wedding dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridesmaids attend a bride at her wedding and often carry the trailing back of her gown.

clue.text: Closure of pub in old hamlet somehow put on hold

indicators.note: the closure of a word is where it ends, so just its last letter is used
somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of pub

explanation.surface: The village pub in an old hamlet has shut down, its future put on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mothballed has been stored away unused and its development suspended for the time being.

clue.text: Drink for drunk not starting to get cold during snooze

indicators.note: not starting means the word loses its opening letter
something happening during another thing falls within it

blocks.note: a nap is a snooze
tight is slang for drunk
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A drink for a drunk who is starting to feel cold while dozing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not starting to get cold' tempts you to read 'not starting' with 'to get'; it belongs to drunk, and 'to get' merely joins in cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is an alcoholic drink taken just before going to bed.

clue.text: Best-dressed males standing trial

indicators.note: standing means upright, and in a down clue a word stood up reads from the bottom

blocks.note: rams are male sheep
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Smartly dressed men standing in the dock at their trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing trial' reads as one courtroom phrase, but 'standing' acts on the males and the trial is separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Smartest is the superlative of smart, meaning most stylishly and neatly turned out in clothing.

clue.text: Republican in reflective frame of mind visiting downtrodden individual

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read back to front
one piece in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a mood is a frame of mind
R is the abbreviation for Republican
visiting somewhere means being at it

explanation.surface: A Republican in a thoughtful mood goes to see someone who is down on their luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective' reads as thoughtful, but here it mirrors the word for frame of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is figuratively a person who lets others walk all over them, a pushover.

clue.text: Noah may be relaxed about source of gopher wood

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, so only its first letter is used
relaxed letters are loosened from their order and can settle into a new one
about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of gopher

explanation.surface: Noah, at ease, considers the gopher wood from which God told him to build the ark.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis the ark is made of gopher wood, so the surface reads as Bible lore; 'wood' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a hard reddish-brown tropical timber used for fine furniture.

clue.text: Elevated position embraced by parent's artistic movement

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held within its arms, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A parent hugging someone on a podium seems to be the parent's own art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parent's' looks possessive, but the 's is 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dadaism, or Dada, was an early twentieth-century avant-garde art movement that rejected logic and convention.

clue.text: Shopkeeper kneading her bread round remains of fire

indicators.note: kneading works and pummels dough, so the letters are worked into a new shape
round means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: taken as written
ash is what remains after a fire

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper kneads dough for her loaf beside the embers of the oven fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Kneading and bread point to a baker, but the shopkeeper sells sewing goods; a haberdasher is a seller of buttons, thread and ribbons in Britain, of men's clothing in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A haberdasher is a retailer selling small sewing articles or menswear, a particular kind of trader.

clue.text: Like retired Victorian PM maybe after a 13?

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so in this down clue the name reads back upwards

blocks.note: as means like, in comparisons
Sir Robert Peel was Prime Minister early in Victoria's reign; maybe marks him as one example

explanation.surface: Like a Victorian Prime Minister in retirement, perhaps after a nightcap.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 down is NIGHTCAP, and after one you might be sound off; the question mark flags that the definition is by example. 'Retired' also hints at bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is drunk at bedtime, so the likely state that follows is sleeping soundly.

clue.text: Man in garden determined to eradicate insect

indicators.note: to eradicate something is to wipe it out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: adamant means firmly determined
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A gardener resolved to wipe out a bug infestation.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam was the first man, placed by God in the Garden of Eden.

clue.text: Style worn by new Danish king

indicators.note: something worn by another is wrapped around it like clothing, so that piece goes inside

blocks.note: a cut is a style, of clothing or hair
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fashionable new look sported by the King of Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Cnut, also called Canute, was an eleventh-century Danish ruler who also became king of England.

clue.text: Traditional story about collecting a penny tax in Anglo-Saxon England

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read from right to left
collecting means taking in, so the word gathers another piece inside

blocks.note: a legend is a traditional story
taken as written
d was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: An old tale about someone collecting a penny in tax in Saxon times.
explanation.walkthrough: LEGEND reversed is DNEGEL; it takes in A after its first letter and adds the penny at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Danegeld was a levy raised by English kings to pay off or defend against Viking raiders.

clue.text: Water found in edges of Charlie's hat

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters
a thing found in another is located inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Charlie
a loch is a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Water discovered along the brim of Charlie's hat after the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Charlie's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is a close-fitting bell-shaped women's hat popular in the 1920s.

clue.text: Rebel with pointed object intercepting letter from abroad to the Queen

indicators.note: to intercept is to come between, so this piece goes in the middle of the others

blocks.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
a tine is a prong of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: An insurgent with a knife stops a foreign letter being delivered to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutineer is someone who rebels against authority, especially sailors rising against a ship's captain.

clue.text: Dictator imprisoning Sudanese leader in warehouse

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front
to imprison is to shut something inside, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: a depot is a storage warehouse
the first letter of Sudanese

explanation.surface: A tyrant locking up an African leader in a storehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler holding absolute power, often used cruelly, which is what a dictator is.
